newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Leader Lott says Republicans want tax cut.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Leader Lott says Republicans want tax cut.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Senate Republicans were united behind wanting tax cuts as part of a balanced budget.

"How big the tax cut package will be will depend on what we're able to do with the overall budget. It would help if we had the president's involvement, it would help if we could get an agreement on a number of issues in the budget," Lott said. He told reporters he hoped there would be a "significant amount" of tax relief, but said he was unable yet to give a figure as to what that might be.
"United Republican position ... in the Senate and in the House is to pursue permanent tax relief ... this year," Lott, a Mississippi Republican said.

"I'm not an advocate of delaying it, but I am an advocate of recognizing that we have to get a budget agreement, we need to have the president's involvement to be able to get that early, we need for it to be bipartisan in the House and the Senate," Lott said.
Asked whether he was saying it may be necessary to delay the tax bill, Lott said, "no that's not what I'm saying."
